pages.title: Moderators
pages.text: Reactor Moderators, commonly and incorrectly called Reactor Coolants, are materials placed $(thing)inside$() a reactor during construction.$(br2)When the reactor runs, a moderator changes the way it performs depending on its properties. Air is a moderator too, just a bad one, so an empty reactor still works.

pages.title: The four properties
pages.text: $(li)$(thing)Absorption$(): the speed at which radiation is absorbed and converted to case heat.$(li)$(thing)Efficiency$(): how efficiently absorbed radiation is converted into heat.$(li)$(thing)Moderation$(): the effectiveness at which radiation is moderated, or softened.$(li)$(thing)Conductivity$(): how well heat is transferred from the fuel rods to the reactor casing.

pages.title: Reading the numbers
pages.text: In general higher values are always better. Absorption is the exception: it may be better or worse depending on your reactor design.$(br2)High absorption soaks radiation up close to the rods, which suits a small dense core. Low absorption lets radiation travel further and fertilize other fuel rods, which suits a large core with room between the columns.

pages.title: Graphite
pages.text: The classic reactor moderator, and the cheapest one worth using. Low absorption with strong moderation, so radiation travels far and comes back softened.$(br2)If you are not sure what to fill a reactor with, fill it with graphite.

pages.title: Ludicrite
pages.text: The end game moderator this mod ships. High absorption, high efficiency, strong moderation and excellent conductivity all at once.$(br2)It is also the best turbine coil in the mod, so expect to make a lot of it.

pages.title: Adding your own
pages.text: Modpack authors can add or modify moderators through data maps or KubeJS, so the list is not fixed.$(br2)For an accurate list of supported blocks and fluids in your pack, open $(thing)JEI$() and check the uses for the Reactor Terminal.
